Empirical Research Plan: 2000–2005 Japanese Cost-Sharing Reform

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Method: LOCAL FUZZY REGRESSION-DISCONTINUITY DESIGN (FRD) with 2SLS implementation.

Rationale
• The coinsurance rate (patient cost sharing) drops discretely at a known statutory birthday (70 years) but the running variable—exact age in months—remains continuous.  
• Because some enrollees may face supplementary employer plans or special exemptions, treatment status (actual coinsurance rate) is not perfectly deterministic; therefore the design is “fuzzy,” with the age threshold serving as an instrument for the actual cost-sharing rate.  
• The FRD isolates a Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) for individuals near the 70-year threshold, which answers the policy question for the marginal patient affected by the law.

Extensions (robustness):  
(1) Panel RD (within-individual before/after turning 70) to soak up individual heterogeneity.  
(2) RD-in-time falsification (placebo at 69 or 71).  
(3) Difference-in-RD exploiting the 2001 revision that partially raised the post-70 coinsurance—treated vs. pre-2001 cohorts.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control Definition
────────────────────────────────────────
Running variable: A_i  = exact age in months on the visit/claim date.  
Cutoff: c = 70 × 12 = 840 months.

Binary instrument (Z_i):  1{A_i ≥ c}.

Treatment variable (D_i): Actual coinsurance rate faced by the patient on visit i, expressed as a proportion of total bill (e.g. 0.30 vs. 0.10).

Treated observations: visits with lower cost sharing (D_i ≤ 0.15).  
Control observations: visits with standard cost sharing (D_i = 0.30) for patients just below 70.

Timing: The threshold is “always on.” Observation window is 2000–2005; we keep visits within, say, ±24 months of 70 for the main specification, and explore bandwidth choice with Imbens-Kalyanaraman and Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik (CCT) selectors.

Outcome families:  
• Utilization Y₁: number of outpatient visits per month, days in hospital, prescription counts.  
• Health status Y₂: 30-day readmission, mortality within 1 y, blood pressure control, etc.  
• Financial risk Y₃: out-of-pocket spending, spending variance, exceeding catastrophic cap.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────
A1 Continuity of potential outcomes: In absence of the cost-sharing drop, expected Y would evolve smoothly through age 70. Plausibility: aging is gradual; no other national policy (e.g., pension eligibility) changes exactly at 70 in Japan (pension age is 65).  
A2 No precise manipulation of age: Impossible to sort around one’s 70th birthday.  
A3 First-stage relevance: The law produces a sizable discrete fall in average coinsurance at 70. Testable.  
A4 Exclusion restriction (FRD): Crossing age 70 influences outcomes only through cost sharing. Potential concern: retirement patterns at 60-65, not 70; senior-citizen discounts on transport at 70 unlikely to affect health utilization within months.  
A5 Monotonicity: No patient faces a higher coinsurance because of the threshold.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats and Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────
T1 Health deteriorates mechanically with age, risking a spurious jump.  
  • Mitigation: narrow bandwidth; flexible polynomials in age; symmetric local linear RD.  
  • Covariate continuity tests (pre-diagnosis health stock, lagged utilization).

T2 Concurrent age-70 programs (municipal subsidies, voluntary check-ups).  
  • Collect municipality-level subsidy data; include fixed effects or drop cities with add-on programs; test for discontinuities in non-price amenities (e.g., influenza voucher take-up).  

T3 Sample composition/measurement: Claims may be missing for decedents or people changing insurers at retirement.  
  • Use panel structure to keep same individuals before/after 70; show RD on enrollment probability and insuree exits; re-weight via inverse probability weighting.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# Libraries -------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)      # fast load/manipulate
library(fixest)          # fast IV / FE regressions
library(rdrobust)        # RD inference
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------
claims <- fread("japan_health_claims_2000_2005.csv")

# 2. Construct variables -----------------------------------------------
claims[, dob := as.Date(dob)]                 # date of birth
claims[, visit_date := as.Date(visit_date)]
claims[, age_months := floor(as.numeric(difftime(visit_date, dob, 
                                     units = "days"))/30.4375)]

cutoff <- 70*12
claims[, above70 := as.integer(age_months >= cutoff)]

# Actual coinsurance assumed in variable 'coins_rate'
# Create treatment indicator: low cost sharing (≤15%)
claims[, low_cs := as.integer(coins_rate <= 0.15)]

# Centered running var
claims[, age_c := (age_months - cutoff)/12]   # in years

# Keep main bandwidth (±24 months)
main <- claims[abs(age_months - cutoff) <= 24]

# 3. First-stage and reduced-form --------------------------------------
fs  <- feols(low_cs ~ above70 + poly(age_c,1), data = main, weights = wgt)
rf  <- feols(out_visits ~ above70 + poly(age_c,1), data = main, weights = wgt)

# 4. Two-stage least squares (fuzzy RD) --------------------------------
iv  <- feols(out_visits ~ 1 | low_cs ~ above70 + poly(age_c,1), 
             data = main, weights = wgt, vcov = "HC3")
summary(iv)

# 5. rdrobust equivalent (local linear) --------------------------------
y  <- main$out_visits
x  <- main$age_months - cutoff
rd <- rdrobust(y, x, c = 0, fuzzy = main$low_cs)
summary(rd)

# 6. Robustness: alternative bandwidth 12 months -----------------------
bw12 <- main[abs(age_months - cutoff) <= 12]
iv12 <- feols(out_visits ~ 1 | low_cs ~ above70 + poly(age_c,1), 
              data = bw12, vcov = "HC3")
etable(iv, iv12)

# 7. Covariate balance check ------------------------------------------
covars <- c("sex","prefecture","baseline_morbidity_index")
bal   <- lapply(covars, function(v)
         feols(as.formula(paste0(v," ~ above70 + poly(age_c,1)")), 
               data = main))
lapply(bal, summary)
```

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results (Prior)
────────────────────────────────────────
• Utilization: A 70-year-old facing a coinsurance cut from 30 % to 10 % is expected to increase outpatient visits by roughly 10–20 %.  
• Health outcomes: Small improvements in management of chronic conditions and slight fall in avoidable hospitalizations; mortality effects likely near zero over a 1-3 y horizon.  
• Risk protection: Mean annual out-of-pocket spending should fall by ≈ 20 k ¥ (about US $180 in 2000 dollars) and its variance should decline.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
────────────────────────────────────────
C1 Density of running variable smooth at cutoff ………………… 1  
C2 Predetermined covariates smooth at cutoff …………………… 1  
C3 Functional-form & bandwidth robustness demonstrated …… 1  
C4 No other discontinuous policies at 70 ………………………… 0.5  
C5 First stage strong; monotonicity plausible …………………… 1  

Total ≈ 4.5 / 5 → high internal validity, residual concern about other age-70 programs.

────────────────────────────────────────
End of plan.
